subject: Service Interruption — Executive Brief & Bridge Notes (BrightWave Analytics)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T09:08:13-07:00
Subject: [SEV-2] 500s spike affecting Hosted inference for BrightWave

Team —

We are seeing an elevated rate of 500 responses from the hosted inference cluster serving BrightWave (customer tag: BW-01). Initial telemetry shows a sudden routing error at the gateway layer at 09:02 PT, affecting ~18% of requests for BrightWave’s production model set. Impact: increased latency and transient failures for production traffic; BrightWave reported errors in their monitoring a few minutes ago.

I’m standing up a short bridge. Please join: Zoom link (internal only): https://zoom.redwood/bridge-sev2-0310.

Immediate asks:
- Grace: can you confirm whether any deploys or routing changes occurred in the last 30m?
- Hannah: start capturing request IDs and earliest 500 traces — attach to incident-status-log.txt.
- Vivek: look at gateway scaling and routing tables; do we have a failing HAProxy node?

I’ll craft the first external touchpoint after we have initial scope. Keep replies on thread; escalate new findings in the bridge.

— Sean
Head of Customer Reliability (acting)
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T09:12:45-07:00
Subject: Re: [SEV-2] 500s spike affecting Hosted inference for BrightWave

On Tue, 10 Mar 2026 at 09:08, Sean Gallagher wrote:
> Team —
>
> We are seeing an elevated rate of 500 responses from the hosted inference cluster serving BrightWave...

Joined the bridge. No deploys in the last hour from infra. I’m seeing a routing flap on az-us-west-2b that is dropping TLS handshakes to one of the gateway instances (gw-azb-7). Recreating the listener appears to temporarily reduce errors.

Action taken: removed gw-azb-7 from the LB pool (09:10 PT), traffic shifted to healthy nodes. Error rate dropped to ~6% but not fully resolved. Hannah is uploading traces now.

Next: I recommend we keep the instance out of rotation and watch for stabilization for 15 minutes, then gradually reintroduce.

— Grace
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T09:28:02-07:00
Subject: Re: [SEV-2] 500s spike affecting Hosted inference for BrightWave

Uploading the first bundle to the incident log. Attached: incident-status-log.txt (contains request IDs, sample traces, and correlation ids).

Observations: many 500s correlate to TLS handshake errors between the gateway and inference workers after the gateway's kernel TLS cache was cleared (likely due to recent config churn). 500s often show up when a connection attempt times out during handshake — not the model stack.

I’ll keep pulling logs and can prepare the timeline for the customer message.

— Hannah
SRE
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Team <ops@brightwave.com>, Maria Santos <maria.santos@brightwave.com>
Cc: CISO <ciso@brightwave.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T10:02:41-07:00
Subject: Customer Update: Service Disruption (BrightWave) — Status & Next Steps

Maria / BrightWave ops —

First, thank you for flagging the issue. I’m Sean Gallagher, and I’m coordinating our response. We opened an internal bridge at 09:06 PT and have been working continuously with our SRE and platform teams. This is an interim executive update while we work to stabilize traffic.

Current status (10:00 PT):
- Impact: transient 500s and increased latency for inference calls from BrightWave’s production service; roughly 15–18% of requests were affected at peak.
- Root cause (investigating): early signs point to a gateway TLS handshake failure tied to one gateway instance (gw-azb-7). The model serving stack appears healthy; errors are surfacing at the routing/gateway layer.
- Mitigation applied: we removed the suspect gateway from rotation at ~09:10 PT; error rate reduced to ~6% and continues trending down.

Immediate next steps:
1) Continue monitoring for 30 minutes before incremental reintroduction of the instance.
2) We will run a rolling validation across the remaining gateway fleet and check TLS session cache behavior to prevent recurrence.
3) Post-incident follow-up: we will share a draft postmortem within 48 hours that includes timeline, root cause analysis, and planned hardening actions.

If you need to escalate to your leadership or security team, please let me know and I’ll schedule a short briefing.

Attachments: incident-status-log.txt (summary of traces and request ids).

We understand the disruption this causes BrightWave’s service and apologize for the impact. I will send another update at +60m or sooner if there’s any material change.

Best,

Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability (acting)
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@brightwave.com>, Ops Team <ops@brightwave.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T12:34:55-07:00
Subject: RE: Customer Update: Service Disruption (BrightWave) — Final Update & Postmortem Plan

Maria / BrightWave —

Final status (12:30 PT): traffic stabilized after we kept the affected gateway out of rotation and applied a temporary fix to TLS session cache settings. Error rate returned to baseline (~0.3%). We reintroduced gw-azb-7 in a controlled fashion at 11:40 PT and continued validation for 30m.

Follow-up and timeline:
- Postmortem draft: we will share an initial postmortem (postmortem-draft.pdf) and timeline within 48 hours. That document will include root cause, mitigation steps we performed, corrective actions, and a proposed timeline for permanent fixes.
- Request for BrightWave input: if you have specific telemetry or request-ids you want us to prioritize in the postmortem, please reply with those IDs or send them to ops@brightwave.com.
- Preventative measures: immediate plan includes a hardening change to gateway TLS cache handling, additional health checks for the gateway listener, and an automated rollback trigger when handshake failures exceed threshold.

Thanks again for your patience. If you’d like an executive call to walk through the timeline and remediation plan, we can schedule one today or tomorrow.

—I’ll follow up with the postmortem link when it’s ready.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability (acting)
Redwood Inference
Attachment: postmortem-draft.pdf (internal draft)
